html:
The Hussite Wars were fought from 1419 to 1434 between the followers of the burned reformer Jan Hus in Bohemia and Catholic armies of the emperor Sigismund and the Pope, which launched five crusades against them.

They began with the first defenestration of Prague in 1419, when Hussites threw councillors out of a town hall window. Led by Jan Žižka, a one eyed and later blind general, peasant armies used wagons chained into forts and early handguns to beat knights again and again. The radical Taborites were crushed by moderate Hussites at Lipany in 1434. The moderates won the right to give communion in both bread and wine. Bohemia stayed mostly Hussite until the Habsburgs reimposed Catholicism after the White Mountain.
sum: The Hussite Wars were fought from 1419 to 1434 between the followers of the burned reformer Jan Hus in Bohemia and Catholic armies of the emperor Sigismund and the Pope, which launched five crusades against them.
